# PR #3117 hosted dispatch comparison — 2026-09-08

**Verdict: INCONCLUSIVE. Do not merge or set the performance gate to PASS.** The complete same-VM A1/B/A2 run verifies correctness and substantial isolated dispatch improvements, but it does not satisfy all protected metrics or required scope.

- Synchronous batch maximum latency is 396.452168 ms for B versus 358.647207/359.167605 ms for A1/A2: +10.541%/+10.381%, above the predeclared 5% tolerance. Control drift is only +0.145%. This is an unresolved protected-metric loss signal; CPU and allocation improvements do not offset it.
- Every loaded process records measured JIT activity (1–112 compilations) after more than 120 seconds of actual workload warmup. The counters do not attribute methods or prove these events caused the latency losses. All samples remain included.
- Several loaded controls drift beyond their CPU or latency tolerances; two microbenchmark controls exceed 2% mean-time drift. Pending-batch maximum latency also loses 6.458% against A2 amid 19.498% maximum-latency control drift.
- Loaded error/recovery/shutdown performance and long-run stability remain unmeasured. Final stop checks begin after processing completes and cannot substitute for shutdown under load.
- One fresh process per configuration per phase limits uncertainty estimates for loaded tails. Millions of correlated messages are not independent process replications. This experiment does not establish equivalence.

## Provenance and scope

[Hosted run](https://github.com/thomhurst/Dekaf/actions/runs/34176568856), one `ubuntu-latest` job, Ubuntu 24.04 image `20260831.293.1`, AMD EPYC 7763, 4 logical CPUs / 2 cores, SDK 10.0.400, runtime 10.0.11, Release, workstation GC.

| Role | Exact SHA |
|---|---|
| baseline | `5df2f0d03607389384b5c1466e17812a9084fac9` |
| candidate | `2a550007ccb091e8f2bf9275a7646277e984dff8` |
| harness | `7614406221b63c0b758f25e0722c8a3bf3ef9d0f` |

The candidate contains the pinned main baseline. Remote main remains that SHA when assessed on 2026-09-08. The assessment implementation is separately pinned at `fb203ddf061703a2f86fb3eca366783aacbb6854`. This report branch inherits the replacement benchmark workflow and **must not be merged into the product**.

Both products and all smoke fixtures were validated before timing. The common microbenchmark fixture uses `CreateBatchProcessor` on both revisions, retaining automatic completion. Microbenchmarks use `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`, CPU 2, at least 20 seconds of direct workload warmup, 30 timed BDN workload warmups targeting one second, and 25 measured iterations with `DontRemove` and `[MemoryDiagnoser]`. Each lifetime processes 262,144 typed integer records, capacity 128 and concurrency 2.

Loaded workloads use tiered compilation, `DOTNET_GCDynamicAdaptationMode=0`, four partitions, 256-byte payloads, capacity 128, concurrency 2 and maximum batch size 16. Broker, baseline producer and consumer use CPUs 0, 1 and 2/3 respectively. Each phase starts a fresh Kafka 4.3.1 broker; each mode uses a fresh topic/process. Synchronous modes offer 50,000 records/s with 1,024 keys; pending modes offer 1,000 records/s with two keys per partition and groups of 32 records. All pacing debt and all raw latency samples are preserved.

Each loaded process offers 121 seconds of warmup and 120 seconds of measured work. Latency starts at scheduled producer offer and ends after handler processing, including pending delay, before automatic frontier bookkeeping. CPU and allocations cover the consumer process between first and last measured completion, including sampler and handler simulation. Pending handlers use `Task.Delay(1)` once per invocation; their allocation is included. Broker/producer CPU is outside this consumer scope. Completed throughput at fixed offered load is not maximum capacity.

## Runtime, batching and correctness

Every synchronous process completes 6,050,000 warmup and 6,000,000 measured messages; every pending process completes 121,000 warmup and 120,000 measured messages. Producer sent/acknowledged counts match, no failures/duplicates/key reordering are reported, final backlog and pending handlers are zero, and every partition has the exact broker-confirmed committed offset. All raw measured latencies were rechecked against reported p50/p99/max and all completion-series counts reconcile.

## Retention and next decision

Artifact `dispatch-3117-34176568856` / ID `10038956322` contains 560,949,854 compressed bytes. Its downloaded ZIP SHA-256 matches the uploaded digest `9f78c91b12c0b62a40ab1dcc3d363f437c1ec53ff69f0a7e05059678fbe6e5e1`. All **6,663 original inventory entries** verify, including hidden files and the exact product/host DLL bindings. The raw ZIP, extracted files, workflow log, metadata, assessment and runtime diagnostics are retained outside removable worktrees at:

`C:/git/Dekaf-evidence/pr-3117/hosted-current-20260908/run-34176568856/`

The artifact retains product source ZIPs, generated fixture/worker sources, loaded binaries, all BDN logs/results, measured and warmup latency arrays, runtime time series, broker/client logs and correctness outputs. The separately archived assessment tool retains its exact source. GitHub artifact retention is 30 days; the local archive is the durable copy.

The preceding completed campaign `34150400216` measured different product/baseline/harness pins and used insufficient warmup and incomplete runtime/pending-handler instrumentation. Its absolute values are not like-for-like controls for this campaign. Run `34175751899` failed in smoke before A1; its driver correction did not repeat a measured run. There is no accepted same-configuration predecessor to use as an extra control.

No further identical paid run is dispatched. Before another full comparison, investigate the measured runtime transitions and the synchronous-batch maximum-latency loss with bounded, method-attributed diagnostics; do not presume a longer warmup alone fixes them. Validate any revised experiment before funding it. Full acceptance also needs the remaining loaded lifecycle/error and stability coverage. Keep the exact product gate failing and preserve these losses alongside the gains. No maintainer tradeoff approval is recorded.
